name: Speech and communication with MND
description: MND-specific guidance for preparing for speech changes, adjusting when speech gets harder, and staying connected without speech.
care_team_notes: Act early with speech pathology, the state MND association, occupational therapy and funding supports so tools can be trialled before speech becomes unreliable.

name: Augmentative and alternative communication
description: Australian speech pathology guidance on low-tech, high-tech and multimodal AAC, including speech-generating devices, communication boards, apps, switches and eye-gaze access.
care_team_notes: A speech pathologist should help assess communication goals, physical access, partner support, environments, fatigue, cognition and future progression.

name: Voice and message banking
description: Planning guidance for preserving personal voice/messages for later use with communication devices and apps.
care_team_notes: Discuss voice banking early, before speech changes become severe; include family messages, emergency phrases, identity words and personally meaningful sounds where possible.

name: Funding a communication system
description: Funding considerations for communication systems, including MND association support, NDIS, My Aged Care and assistive technology pathways.
care_team_notes: Capture the functional communication need, urgency, progression risk, trials completed, access method and clinical recommendations in funding evidence.

name: Communication partner and carer strategies
description: Practical strategies for carers and communication partners, including waiting, checking understanding, yes/no systems, partner-assisted scanning and quiet environments.
care_team_notes: Train family and paid carers in the person’s preferred yes/no signals, repair strategies, access method, care alerts, emergency phrases and dignity-preserving communication.

name: Speech and swallowing overlap
description: Speech changes can occur alongside swallowing changes, especially in bulbar MND, so communication and swallowing support often need coordinated speech pathology input.
care_team_notes: Ask speech pathology to review both speech/communication and swallowing safety when speech becomes slurred, soft, effortful or tiring.
